gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured surge let-through: Wirecutter hit each strip with a 5,000 V surge and measured 182.8 V average let-through on the Eaton Tripp Lite Protect It 12-outlet TLP1208SAT. The same test put the Isobar6Ultra/Isobar8Ultra at about 200 V, so ChatGPT's $130.71 'heavy-duty' Isobar6Ultra pick did no better than the cheap 12-outlet Protect It.
standout_why: I opened honestfred.com (rank 2/4), rottenwifi.com (rank 8/6) and techgearlab.com (rank 11/13). None of them gives a measured let-through or surge figure. Honestfred repeats Wirecutter's TLP1208SAT pick and Tom's Guide's 2,100 J rating but says it tested nothing. Rottenwifi lists only maker ratings (Belkin 330 V, Eaton TLP606B 500 V) and joules. TechGearLab (updated 2023-12-19, tested by Ian Nicholson) gives scores and spec-sheet joules but explicitly no let-through numbers. I could not open the two cited rivals (goodhousekeeping.com and tomsguide.com: the fetch tool was blocked or got only the title), so I can't confirm they lack a measurement. Both ChatGPT answers cite them only for picks and joules. Both answers use joules as the yardstick ('2,000J+'), and no result separates rated figures from measured ones.
decides: This confirms a 12-outlet Eaton Tripp Lite Protect It as the pick for protection per dollar. In Wirecutter's test it let through less than half of its 400 V UL rating, and it measured slightly lower than the metal Isobar6Ultra, which ChatGPT showed at $130.71. That weakens the 'heavy-duty' case for the Isobar unless you need the metal housing. It also undercuts ranking by joules: no lab measurement exists for ChatGPT's top 'value' pick, the Anker 2,100 J strip, or for the Belkin 12-outlet, so those picks rest on ratings only. Caveat: the only copy of these numbers I could open is a 2024 mirror of Wirecutter's guide, and one mirror names the 12-outlet pick TLP1208TELTV instead, so the model may have changed. Check Wirecutter's current page before publishing.
